question: What does the eigenvalue tell you about what happens to an eigenvector?
direct_answer: It tells you the scaling factor along that direction.
expanded_answer: If λ is greater than 1, the eigenvector is stretched; if it is between 0 and 1, it is shrunk; if it is negative, the vector is flipped and scaled. So the eigenvalue encodes how the transformation acts along that special direction.
key_points: Magnitude of λ gives stretch or shrink
It describes action along the eigenvector direction
common_wrong_ideas: Thinking λ only measures length and never sign
